summary: Wilde told Reginald Turner that 'your little friend Alphonse' had been arrested for blackmail, and added that he was 'quite an imp, though attractive in love-scenes'.

sources.quote: Your little friend Alphonse was arrested last night for chantage. He demanded fifteen francs, and was only given ten and a cab-fare, so on being expelled from the house he made a scene and was taken up. There is much joy amongst his friends, as his general conduct did not meet with approval. It is a pity he always wanted to behave badly; it gave him a demoniac pleasure. He was quite an imp, though attractive in love-scenes.
sources.context: Wilde to Reginald Turner, Tuesday [postmark 6 December 1898], Hôtel d'Alsace, Paris (MS Hyde) - the whole of the Alphonse paragraph. The editors gloss 'chantage' as blackmail. The folio is A census of the paris exile household in December 1898 and form one: Sir John Ashton and his 'little friend' Joseph (both already on this map, connected on this same page), Turner's 'little friend' Alphonse, and Hylton with 'his boy' Herbert. Four young men in three sentences, all described to Wilde's closest correspondent in the same possessive formula.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That Alphonse was Turner's, and what Wilde thought of him.
